title: An affine parameter family of sections on a smooth integral group
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $H/k$ a smooth integral separated group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. There exist an integer $d\geq0$, a nonempty affine open subscheme $V\subseteq\mathbf A^d_k$, where $\mathbf A^d_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], and an invertible module $\mathcal M$ on $H\times_kV$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-sc-invertible-module], with the following properties. For $v\in V(k)$ put $\mathcal M_v=i_v^*\mathcal M$, where $i_v:H\to H\times_kV$ sends $h$ to $(h,v)$ and pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is a family of sections $(s_v)_{v\in V(k)}$, with $s_v\in\Gamma(H,\mathcal M_v)$, such that for every $v\in V(k)$ the open $H_{s_v}$ is affine, where $H_{s_v}$ is the locus where the value of $s_v$ in the residue-field fibre is nonzero [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every $h\in H(k)$ there is a $v\in V(k)$ such that $h\in H_{s_v}$. No constancy of the isomorphism classes of the $\mathcal M_v$ is asserted.

This extracts a parameter family, not the final ample module.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq H$ from an affine cover; $H$ is nonempty because it is integral. Apply the affine-boundary lemma to obtain an effective Cartier divisor $D$ with $H\setminus|D|=U$. The canonical-section lemma gives an invertible module $L=\mathcal O_H(D)$ and $a\in\Gamma(H,L)$ with zero scheme $D$. In a local frame $a$ is multiplication by the equation of $D$, so $H_a=U$.

source.place: Tag 0BF7, groupoids-lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective, smooth irreducible case, finite-chart construction and norm footnote, before rational-equivalence-for-Pic.

proof.text: Apply the finite-chart lemma to $X=H$, obtaining $d,n,j:W\hookrightarrow H,q:W\to V$. Put $Y=H\times_k W$, $Z=H\times_k V$, $p=1_H\times q$, and $\alpha:Y\to H$, $\alpha(h,w)=h j(w)$. Multiplication and $j$ define this morphism by the group-scheme data. The pullback clause of the finite-locally-free descent lemma makes $p$ finite locally free of degree $n$. Its fibre algebra at every point has dimension $n\geq1$, hence is a nonzero finite algebra over a field and has a maximal ideal; every fibre has a point, so $p$ is surjective. Apply the function-norm lemma to $p$ to obtain restriction-compatible multiplicative norms with the scalar-power and residue-zero properties. Pull back $L,a$ along $\alpha$, giving the invertible module $A=\alpha^*L$ and section $b=\alpha^*a$; its nonvanishing locus is $Y_b=\alpha^{-1}(U)$ by the residue-fibre formula. The existing norm-of-invertible-sections lemma, with exponent $1$, now gives an invertible module $\mathcal M$ on $Z$ and a section $t\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal M)$ with $$Z_t=\{z\in Z:p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq\alpha^{-1}(U)\}.$$

source.place: Tag 0BF7, groupoids-lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective, smooth irreducible case, finite-chart construction and norm footnote, before rational-equivalence-for-Pic.

proof.text: For every $v\in V(k)$ set $s_v=i_v^*t$ in $\mathcal M_v=i_v^*\mathcal M$. Pullback preserves invertibility and nonvanishing opens by its residue-fibre formula. Write $W_v=\coprod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Spec}k$, with points $w_i$, using the chart lemma. The finite-coproduct base-change lemma, applied to this decomposition along $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, identifies $p$ over $H\times\{v\}$ with $n$ copies of $H$; on the $i$th copy $\alpha$ is right translation $R_{j(w_i)}$. Hence Step 2 gives, for all points of $H$, $$H_{s_v}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n R_{j(w_i)}^{-1}(U)=\bigcap_{i=1}^n Uj(w_i)^{-1}.$$ Translation is an isomorphism: its inverse is translation by the group inverse, since the composites are the identity by the group laws. Each displayed open is therefore affine. The diagonal of $H$ is a closed immersion, hence affine by the closed-immersion-finite lemma. Apply the affine-diagonal intersection lemma repeatedly to this nonempty finite family ($n\geq1$) to conclude that $H_{s_v}$ is affine.

proof.text: Fix $h\in H(k)$. The inverse image $W_h=j^{-1}(h^{-1}U)$ is nonempty open in $W$: both $j(W)$ and $h^{-1}U$ are nonempty open in the irreducible space $H$. It is dense in $W$, since a nonempty open subspace of an irreducible space is irreducible. Thus $T_h=W\setminus W_h$ is closed nowhere dense. Apply the finite-image lemma to $q$ to see that $q(T_h)$ is closed nowhere dense in $V$. Consequently $V_h=V\setminus q(T_h)$ is nonempty open. Since $V$ is locally of finite type over $k$, the Jacobson lemma gives a closed point of $V$ in $V_h$ (apply density to the closed subset $V$ itself). The residue-field lemma makes it a $k$-rational point $v$. Every point $w_i$ above $v$ belongs to $W_h$, so $h j(w_i)\in U$ for all $i$. The formula of Step 3 yields $h\in H_{s_v}$. The fixed $d,V,\mathcal M$ and the pullbacks $s_v=i_v^*t$ satisfy every clause of the item.

Tensor pullback preserves invertibility and nonvanishing loci by its residue-fibre formula; needed for alpha and every fibre inclusion.
The separatedness hypothesis makes the diagonal a closed immersion, so this general lemma makes it affine.
